Requirements: CMake ≥ 3.5, a C11 and C++17 compiler, Python 3, git, and ninja (optional, `GEN=ninja`)
and uv for the Python checks.

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules <repo> && cd duck-changepoint
GEN=ninja make release   # builds DuckDB v2.0.0 from the submodule, then build/release/extension/cpt/cpt.duckdb_extension
```

These checks gate CI:

```sh
make test_release     # SQL logic tests in DuckDB's unittest
make test_core        # C tests of the numerical core under ASan/UBSan
make test_threads     # the core on 8 threads under ThreadSanitizer
make leak_check       # every function under macOS `leaks`, against this tree's debug build
make crap             # CRAP < 10 for every C and C++ function (lizard + llvm-cov)
```

These are run by hand:

```sh
make compare_ruptures   # 200 random series against ruptures
make check_optimality   # PELT against unpruned Optimal Partitioning
make bench              # timings above
make joern_leaks        # static allocation/release audit with Joern
```

See [DEVELOPMENT.md](/development/) and [docs/TESTING.md](/development/testing/).

## Reference data against R changepoint

The comparison with R's changepoint package on Nile, Lai2005fig4, wave.c44137 and ftse100 lives in a
separate repository, [hugr-lab/duck-changepoint-reference](https://github.com/hugr-lab/duck-changepoint-reference), because three of those datasets are distributed with
changepoint under the GPL. With both repositories checked out side by side:

```sh
cd ../duck-changepoint-reference
make test                         # against the extension built in ../duck-changepoint
make reference-data               # regenerate the data with R changepoint in a container
```



## Toolchain

- CMake ≥ 3.5, a C11 and C++17 compiler (clang or gcc; MSVC through the CI toolchain), Python 3, git,
  ninja (optional, `GEN=ninja`), uv for the Python checks.
- No external libraries: libc, libm and DuckDB.
- `duckdb` (v2.0.0) and `extension-ci-tools` are git submodules (`git submodule update --init`).

## Build

```sh
GEN=ninja make release   # DuckDB from the submodule + build/release/extension/cpt/cpt.duckdb_extension
GEN=ninja make debug     # same, debug
```

`make release` is the extension template's build: it compiles DuckDB with the extension linked into
the shell and `unittest`, and writes the loadable binary. The first build takes several minutes; later
ones only recompile what changed. `OVERRIDE_GIT_DESCRIBE=v2.0.0` in the Makefile stamps the version:
DuckDB 2.0 does not read it from git, and without it the binary names the submodule's commit hash and
refuses to load into the released DuckDB. `compile_commands.json` is written to `build/release/`.

`src/cpp/cpt_extension.cpp` is the entry point. It registers the C functions in `src/functions`
through DuckDB's C API on a connection to the loader's database (inside DuckDB a `duckdb_connection` is
a `Connection *`); `src/cpp/cpt_query.cpp` gives the bind the query, for interrupts. CMakeLists.txt only
builds as part of DuckDB's build.

## DuckDB versions

`main` is built and tested for DuckDB 2.0.0, the `duckdb` submodule. A C++ extension is tied to the
exact DuckDB release it was built against: a new release means moving the submodule, `OVERRIDE_GIT_DESCRIBE`
and `duckdb_version` in `.github/workflows/MainDistributionPipeline.yml`.

The `v1.5.x` branch keeps the stable C API build (headers from v1.5.6 in `duckdb_capi/`, `make
test_compat`), whose one binary loads in every DuckDB from 1.5.6 on. A fix to the core or the SQL
functions that matters for 1.5.x users goes to both branches.

## Tests

See [docs/TESTING.md](/development/testing/). Before a commit:

```sh
make release test_release test_core
```

Before a release, also run `make compare_ruptures check_optimality bench leak_check
joern_leaks crap`, and
`make test` in the companion `duck-changepoint-reference` repository (R changepoint comparison).

## Code conventions

- C11, tabs, 120 columns (`.clang-format`). Functions and types are `snake_case` with a `cpt_`
  prefix. SQL callbacks are `CamelCaseFunction` as in the DuckDB template.
- `src/core` must not include DuckDB headers.
- Errors go through `char err[CPT_ERR_LEN]` and a non-zero return, and the SQL layer turns them into
  `duckdb_scalar_function_set_error`. Allocation failures are reported, not ignored.
- No per-iteration allocation in algorithm loops; workspaces are allocated once per call.
- Every new cost or algorithm needs a brute-force counterpart in `test/c/test_core.c`.
- Allocate in `src/core` with `cpt_malloc` / `cpt_calloc` / `cpt_realloc` (`cpt_alloc.h`), so that
  `test_core`'s fault injection covers the out-of-memory path.
- Keep every function at CRAP < 10 (`make crap`, checked in CI). In practice that means cyclomatic
  complexity below 10 and tests for every branch. Prefer small functions that compute a value from their
  arguments (`binseg_pick`, `binseg_done`, `segment_moments`), explicit workspace structs with alloc/free
  pairs, and descriptor tables (`COST_SPECS`, `REGISTRATIONS`) over `switch` chains.
- SQL functions that return segment ends supply a `cpt_bkps_algorithm` to `cpt_execute_bkps`
  (`cpt_call.h`), which owns the row loop, NULL handling, cost creation, the work limit and error
  reporting.

## Layout

The layout follows hugr-lab/mssql-extension:

```
src/            extension sources (core/ and functions/ in C, cpp/ the C++ entry point, include/)
test/sql/       SQLLogicTests (gating)
test/c/         standalone C tests with sanitizers
test/python/    manual cross-checks (ruptures, optimality)
bench/          bench.sql + runner
docs/           architecture, algorithms, costs and penalties, testing
website/        the documentation site (Docusaurus), https://hugr-lab.github.io/duck-changepoint/
```

The site's pages in `website/docs` are generated from README.md, this file and `docs/*.md` by
`website/sync_pages.py`. Edit those sources, then run `python3 website/sync_pages.py` and commit both;
`docs-build.yml` fails a pull request whose pages are out of date. To preview the site:
`cd website && npm ci && npx docusaurus start`.
